newsitem.title: UK: British diplomat guilty in Japanese porn case.
newsitem.headline: British diplomat guilty in Japanese porn case.

text.p: A senior British diplomat was found guilty on Thursday of smuggling a large collection of "depraved" child pornography into Britain from Japan.
Robert Coghlan, 54, who spent 30 years in British embassies around the world, was remanded in custody and will be sentenced on Friday.
Coghlan, who faces up to seven years in jail, showed no reaction apart from biting his lip and shaking his head as the jury returned its unanimous "guilty" verdict after 52 minutes.
He bought much of the paedophile material while serving as first secretary in the information department at the embassy in Tokyo, prosecutors said during his trial in London.
Coghlan was still busy building up his illicit video collection when he helped the Princess of Wales around Tokyo during a visit to Japan in February last year.
He is believed to be the first British diplomat to be found guilty of smuggling pornographic material.

Videos, photographs and magazines considered obscene in Britain but not in Japan were found in Coghlan's belongings during a routine customs search before they were shipped out of Britain to his new posting in Spain.
Prosecutor Nigel Lithman told Southwark Crown Court that 70 videos were found containing scenes of homosexual "paedophilic depravity".

Lithman said: "It would seem that in Japan he had something of a dual existence, that he was something of a Jekyll and Hyde character -- sometimes a respectable representative of the country, at other times visiting specialist sex shops, buying the most profane type of paedophile material, until he had accumulated this large collection."

Coghlan, divorced with two children, had denied the charges. He has been suspended from duty since March. The Foreign Office said: "We will be paying close attention to the outcome of the trial and considering what disciplinary action is needed."
Lithman said the diplomat had deliberately tried to hide his illegal collection although he knew his belongings would be sent through Britain on the way to Madrid.
